body:
Parent regional integration: #484. This bounded neighbor-consistency follow-up is blocked until the supporting source packet #485 is merged.

#485 screens IBC v1.3 section 25, “49th Parallel (Pacific to Columbia Valley),” at 1 km intervals. For 18 consecutive samples, the line is 1–5.9 km from the assigned BC location boundary and the 2021 Statistics Canada CD edge; the same line is within 25 m of a 2024 Washington county edge. Candidate BC features include `atlas:district:CAN-5915:BRC` / CD 5915 and city `gb:CAN:ADM3:43193130B1191968375732`; candidate Washington Census county GEOIDs are 53073 (Whatcom) and 53055 (San Juan). These Washington GEOIDs are source IDs, not asserted WorldAtlas location IDs; resolve the current opposite-side members and release pins during coordination. Full sample, method, sources, release pins and caveats are in #485 `ibc-bc-neighbor-screen.json`.

This is a potentially different treatment of coastal water, not an established boundary error. The IBC data are mapping-only and cannot establish delimitation or ownership. Jointly inspect authoritative BC and Washington land/water coverage, source vintages, and any official boundary/coastal-water representation with both neighbor sides and current pins. Conclude whether the difference is expected water omission, a source-vintage artifact, or requires a coordinated engineering correction. Do not make a unilateral geometry or hierarchy change; preserve existing source material and leave the answer unresolved if authoritative evidence is insufficient.
